sets.label: Reference demo — current state → optimized (synthetic, 200 transcripts)
sets.description: Credential-free run of each optimization lever and the stacked optimized target, with member-ID quality and the combined scorecard. Matches release v0.1.0.
takeaways: Stacking the levers (optimized target) vs the current state: tokens per transcript 25,393 → 12,548 (−50.6%), p95 latency 927 → 457 ms (−50.7%), estimated cost $1,187.61 → $628.00 per month (−47.1%), and modeled HTTP 429 rate 2.0% → 0.2%.
Token reduction alone delivers most of the cost saving (tokens −42.5%, cost −39.2% to $722.40/month), but throttling remains (429 rate 1.4%) because every call still shares one deployment.
Multi-deployment routing removes throttling (429 rate 0.1%, batch 1,260 s → 120 s) but saves less cost (−12.5%) because some tasks route to a pricier model tier.

Quality: member-ID recall rises from 30.8% (naive regex) to 93.5% (deterministic extraction cascade) with 0% false positives and 93.5% precision. The candidate passes the release gate (recall ≥ 90%, precision ≥ 85%, false-positive rate ≤ 10%).
caveats: Synthetic transcripts and a deterministic mock model — no Azure calls. Latency, HTTP 429s, and batch time are modeled by the quota simulation.
Cost is an estimate from the example pricing file, extrapolated from 200 transcripts to 7,000 per day.
The naive baseline evaluation has no gate rules; it is shown for comparison.

sets.label: Architecture options — current state vs Options A/B/C (modeled, 7,000/day)
sets.description: Modeled full-day batch across the assessment options and a single high-quota deployment. Operations and cost only.
takeaways: Current state (one shared 250K-TPM deployment) needs ~11.9 hours to clear 7,000 transcripts with a 2.0% HTTP 429 rate — the throttled baseline.
Option A (quota-aware routing across 4 deployments plus token reduction) cuts the batch to ~1.8 hours and cost to $626.79/month (−46.6%) — the cheapest option.
Option B (task-based routing plus caching) clears the batch in ~44 minutes with a 0.1% 429 rate at $1,031.80/month.
Option C (PTU base plus Standard burst) is as fast as B but the most expensive ($1,750.23/month, +49.2%) — justified only when latency must be guaranteed.
A single high-quota deployment (25M TPM) removes throttling (8 minutes, 0.02% 429s) but leaves cost unchanged ($1,172.91/month) because no tokens are saved.
caveats: Modeled: synthetic transcripts, mock model, and a quota simulation for HTTP 429s and timing — no Azure calls.
Options B and C send some tasks to pricier model tiers in the example pricing file, which is why they cost more than A despite equal token counts.
For measurements on real Azure, choose a “Live Azure” result set.

sets.label: Live Azure (sandbox) — current state vs Option B, 7,000 transcripts each
sets.description: Both configurations run live, back to back, on the same gpt-5.4-nano Global Standard deployment (5M TPM quota) in the author's sandbox on 2026-09-28, with 24 concurrent workers and synthetic transcripts. Latency, tokens, HTTP 429s, retries, and wall clock are all measured.
takeaways: Option B cleared the full day's 7,000 transcripts in 39 minutes vs 1.50 hours for the current state (−56.2%), more than doubling throughput (78.0 → 177.9 transcripts/min).
Per-transcript latency fell: p50 18.0 s → 7.9 s (−56.2%) and p95 23.8 s → 10.1 s (−57.4%).
Tokens per transcript fell from 25,966 to 12,621 (−51.4%), and deterministic extraction removed about 4,750 model calls (35,000 → 30,250).

Neither run was throttled: 0 HTTP 429 responses in 65,253 calls, at 41–45% of the 5M TPM quota. Throughput matched workers ÷ median latency (24 ÷ 18.0 s ≈ 80/min; 24 ÷ 7.9 s ≈ 182/min), so the batch is bound by per-call latency and concurrency, not TPM — cutting per-call work is what made Option B faster.

Estimated cost: $1,302.75 → $931.12 per month (−28.5%) at the pricing file's tier rates. Every call actually hit the same nano deployment; at the nano rate Option B is about $0.0028 vs $0.0062 per transcript (≈55% lower, author's estimate).
Reliability: 3 transient HTTP 500 responses across both runs, all retried successfully; 0 errors.
caveats: Direct mode serves every model tier from one deployment, so Option B's tier routing was not exercised live; the gains come from deterministic extraction, selective context, and fewer calls.
Live latency varies by day: the earlier August run of the same baseline (next result set) had p50 32.6 s. Compare runs from the same session.
Sandbox deployment and synthetic transcripts; not a production measurement. The endpoint hostname is redacted in the bundled files.

observed.note: From the result files, which record observed HTTP 429s, retries, and wall clock. Requests include retries.

sets.label: Live Azure (sandbox) — earlier 7,000-transcript baseline (August, legacy format)
sets.description: An earlier live run of the baseline on the same gpt-5.4-nano deployment (5M TPM quota), 24 workers, synthetic transcripts — recorded before run provenance, so observed figures come from its run logs. Same conclusion as the September runs: no throttling, latency × concurrency bound.
takeaways: All 7,000 transcripts (35,001 model calls) completed in 2.50 hours with zero HTTP 429 responses; one transient HTTP 500 was retried successfully.
The deployment ran at about 1.22M tokens per minute — roughly 24% of its 5M TPM quota — so the quota was not the constraint.
Throughput follows concurrency ÷ per-transcript latency: 24 workers ÷ 32.6 s median ≈ 44 transcripts/min, close to the observed 46.6. Per-call latency and concurrency bound the batch, not TPM.

Smaller runs of the same configuration show lower throughput (25.7 and 37.6 transcripts/min at 30 and 500) because start-up and the final partial wave weigh more; at full volume the worker pool stays busy.
Estimated cost: $0.0074 per transcript, about $1,559 per month at 7,000 per day (pricing-file estimate).
caveats: This file predates run provenance: its TPM (45,858), HTTP 429 rate (0.1%), and batch time (~66.5 h) are modeled and do not reflect the run — use the observed table.
Sandbox deployment and synthetic transcripts; not a production measurement.

observed.note: Derived from the run logs (not bundled because they contain endpoint hostnames). Same configuration at three volumes; each transcript makes 5 model calls.
